claim: A 2-layer attention-only model forms induction heads in layer 1
published: Induction heads need ≥2 layers (Elhage et al. 2021); score defined by Olsson et al. 2022
ours: max layer-1 induction score 0.65 vs 0.031 at random init
criterion: trained max score > 0.3 and > 10× the random-init score

claim: Induction heads causally implement in-context copying
published: Ablating induction heads removes in-context learning in small attn-only models (Olsson et al., Argument 3)
ours: repeat loss 2.68 [2.55, 2.83] → 12.45 [12.33, 12.56] nats when ablated (random-head control 2.64 [2.51, 2.79])
criterion: ablation raises repeat loss by > 1 nat and > 3× the random-head control's increase

published: Induction head keys read a previous-token head's output (Elhage et al. 2021)
ours: ablating prev-token head 0.3 raises repeat loss to 11.22 nats
criterion: ablation raises repeat loss by > 1 nat

claim: Induction heads form abruptly early in training (phase change)
published: ICL score jumps in a narrow window at ~2.5–5B tokens in Anthropic's models (Olsson et al., Argument 1)
ours: Pythia-160M: largest jump in max induction score between 1.07B and 2.10B tokens (0.03 at init → 0.96 final)
criterion: largest single-interval jump occurs before 20B tokens and accounts for > 50% of the total rise
